evals.title: Collective credit and calibrated causality
evidence: `apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/kc-town-hall-funding.ts:218-310` atomizes Jamie's City-listed developer/presenter role, the CCED Board recommendation, Council acceptance and negotiation authority, appropriation, 2024 withdrawal and unused-funds reappropriation, and Jamie's attributed transition; each observation carries an explicit limitation.

`apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/kc-town-hall-funding.ts:313-500` keeps the three claims separate. The funding projection says, “This was authorization, not receipt,” requires the withdrawal/reappropriation ending, and rejects agreement execution, receipt, expenditure, completion, and Jamie-centered causality.

`apps/www/src/content/work/kc-town-hall.mdx:26-55` renders the official funding chain and transition separately, stating, “This is Jamie's approved first-hand account, not a fact established by the City records above,” and declines any inferred relationship to the later withdrawal.

`apps/www/src/data/work.ts:529-595` repeatedly uses “Jamie states” and “Separately, the City,” retains the full unused-funds ending, omits private mechanics, and credits both “Jamie Burkart” and “KC Town Hall LLC collaborators.”

Existing collective-credit governance is consistent: `apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/development-records.ts:606-624` names Jamie's direct Cabaret Law campaign actions while explicitly preserving credit for Rafael Espinal, partner organizations, the Council, and the Mayor.

Read-only verification reproduced the exact candidate fingerprint; `npm run test:knowledge-evals` passed 10/10 tests, `npm run test:citations` passed 9/9, and citation, knowledge-bank, public-safety, and route checks all exited successfully.
evals.recommended_next_move: Preserve the role-versus-government-decision decomposition, first-hand transition boundaries, mandatory unused-funds ending, and collective-credit regression coverage.

evals.title: Source-backed strength through Chad's lens
evidence: `apps/www/src/data/work.ts:529-595` makes Jamie's City-listed role, planning/documentation function, collaborator credit, mission-aligned transition, and candid unused-funds ending immediately legible to hiring readers.

`apps/www/src/content/work/kc-town-hall.mdx:18-61` is purposefully organized around what became usable, what Jamie did, the exact official funding record, the separately attributed transition, and “stewardship through transition.”

`apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/kc-town-hall-funding.ts:368-500` uses exact recommendation, acceptance, appropriation, withdrawal, and reappropriation language without shame or euphemism while excluding private reasons and unsupported transfer mechanics.

Selection is restrained: `apps/www/src/data/work.ts:537-540` marks the project non-featured at priority 6; `docs/knowledge-bank/promotion-slate.md:28-40` selects only three bounded claims; and `apps/www/src/data/proofs.ts:528-575` supplies a concise Technical Operations projection instead of exposing the full bank.

The ending is candid and public-safe: `apps/www/src/data/work.ts:577-595` says the full appropriation remained unused and was reappropriated while expressly omitting private financial, legal, property, banking, and stakeholder circumstances.
findings: The broader statements that Jamie “helped shape redevelopment planning, public-benefit documentation, stakeholder context, and municipal-review support” and made materials usable to collaborators (`apps/www/src/content/work/kc-town-hall.mdx:18-24`) lack a KC-specific atomic observation or concrete artifact/use instance. The structured observations at `apps/www/src/data/knowledge-bank/kc-town-hall-funding.ts:216-310` establish the City-listed role, official chronology, and attributed transition, but not those fuller work-product assertions.
evals.recommended_next_move: Add a bounded KC-specific observation and evidence relationship for the planning/documentation outputs and collaborator use, or narrow those two public paragraphs to the currently structured evidence.
